=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Baseline:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics; AUD 24,000,000; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law

## Threshold point: none of the "[STANDARD]", "FINAL" or "cleared" labels bind us

The Seller's covering material says that:
- clauses marked [STANDARD] were "reviewed and cleared by both sides";
- the package was "settled at principal level";
- the review should "focus only on [OPEN]" items.

These are the counterparty's own negotiating assertions, not agreed terms. We should not treat them as such for four reasons:

- **No issue is actually marked [OPEN].** Accepting the framing would mean accepting the whole package unreviewed.
- **The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts "settled".** Bluefen consent has not been obtained, Riverlark has not been repaid, the privacy incident is "preliminary" and bonuses are missing from the funds flow.
- **The "market context" figures are not neutral.** They are the Seller's opening positions, presented as consensus.
- **Action:** please confirm internally whether Wattlebridge principals agreed anything. Unless they did, every item below should be treated as open. The mark-up should say expressly that the Buyer does not accept the [STANDARD] categorisation.

---

## SPA-N-001: General liability cap (cl 12.1)
- **Seller:** Cap of 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** A cap of 40–50% of price (AUD 9.6m–12m), with a fallback no lower than about 30%. The cap must apply to general warranties only. Fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities and fraud must sit outside it.
- **Recommendation: Reject; counter at 50%.** The known exposures are already material relative to 4.8m: Bluefen at 30% of revenue, Ironquay IP, the privacy incident and AUD 750k+ of unpriced liabilities. W&I insurance could bridge the gap if the Seller won't move.

## SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket (cl 12.2)
- **Seller:** De minimis of AUD 25k (about 0.1%). Basket of AUD 250k (about 1.04%), with only the excess recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer wants:**
  - De minimis of about AUD 10k, with related claims aggregated.
  - Basket of about 0.5% (AUD 120k), operating as a **tipping** basket so recovery runs from the first dollar once it is exceeded.
  - No threshold for fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities or fraud.
- **Recommendation: Reject; counter at 10k / 120k tipping.** A 250k deductible removes recovery for most realistic mid-size warranty losses.

## SPA-N-003: General claims time limit (cl 12.3 / 13)
- **Seller:** 18 months for general claims. Also, any limitation "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer wants:**
  - At least 24 months, so that two full audit cycles fall within the period.
  - Separate periods for tax (expiry of the relevant ATO/OSR amendment period plus 3–6 months, minimum about 5 years) and fundamentals (7 years or the statutory limitation period).
  - The default-application wording deleted.
- **Recommendation: Counter at 24 months and strike the default-application wording.** That wording silently extends 18 months to title, tax and indemnity claims.

## SPA-N-004: Fundamental / Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same 20% cap and 18-month limit "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** Capacity, authority, title and share-capital warranties as Fundamental Warranties, with:
  - a cap of 100% of price;
  - no de minimis or basket;
  - a 7-year limit or the statutory limitation period;
  - no disclosure against them.
- **Recommendation: Reject outright.** If title fails, we have paid AUD 24m for nothing, and recovery would be capped at AUD 4.8m.

## SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** No fraud carve-out. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 (limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance) apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out providing that no limitation, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance provision applies to claims arising from fraud, dishonesty, wilful misconduct or wilful concealment by the Seller or its officers, employees or agents. Claims under ACL s 18 / s 236 should also be preserved to the extent the law does not permit exclusion.
- **Recommendation: Insist; non-negotiable.** The "any nature" drafting purports to cap fraud, and courts may read ambiguity against us on scope.

## SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope (Schedule 7 / DL 1.1–1.2)
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (as at 22 Sept 2026), the Accounts, the statutory registers and all public records.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Specific disclosures only, effective only if **fairly disclosed** with enough detail for the Buyer to identify the nature, scope and quantum of the matter.
  - Data room documents disclosed only to the extent a specific disclosure cross-refers to them.
  - No disclosure against Fundamental Warranties, the tax indemnity or the specific indemnities.
  - No general disclosure of public records beyond ASIC/PPSR searches actually run on a set date.
  - Any update at Completion requires Buyer consent or gives a walk right.
- **Recommendation: Reject general disclosure.** It turns every warranty into a "find it yourself" exercise and would, for example, neutralise warranties on the very issues listed in DL 2–9.

## SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* knew of, "including any matter discoverable" from the data room or public records. This is constructive knowledge.
- **Buyer wants:** A pro-sandbagging clause stating that the Buyer's knowledge (actual, constructive or imputed) does not reduce any claim. Fallback: actual knowledge only, limited to named deal-team individuals, of the specific breach and its likely quantum, excluding advisers.
- **Recommendation: Reject; counter with pro-sandbagging.** Combined with SPA-N-006, the clause would bar claims on everything we diligenced.

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours only. The condition is deemed satisfied on delivery of "the counterparty's written consent." No consent has been obtained (DL 2), and the clause 11.3 conditions are unaddressed.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A Condition Precedent (CP), waivable by the Buyer only, satisfied only by an **unconditional** written consent in a form satisfactory to the Buyer, with all clause 11.3 conditions satisfied and no adverse change to contract terms.
  - The Seller to use best or all reasonable endeavours.
  - A sunset date with a Buyer termination right.
  - A warranty that no notice of termination or non-renewal has been received.
- **Recommendation: Hard CP; reject the "consent delivered = satisfied" wording.** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or 30% of revenue, and a conditional consent could carry adverse terms.

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, with the release to be provided *after* Completion.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - The facility treated as Debt and repaid at Completion out of the price under a payout letter.
  - At Completion: a deed of release, discharge of all security, PPSR releases (including any security over the shares), and a waiver of the change-of-control default under clause 8.1 for the period up to repayment.
  - A specific indemnity for any residual amount.
- **Recommendation: Reject post-Completion release; make discharge a Completion deliverable.** Debt-free means debt-free at Completion. Clause 8.1 would otherwise put the company in default on day one.

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (DD-005 / funds flow)
- **Seller:** AUD 420k of Completion bonuses "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised. Tax and on-costs not addressed (DL 5).
- **Buyer wants:**
  - The AUD 420k plus payroll tax, superannuation guarantee and other on-costs treated as Transaction Costs or Debt, deducted from the price, itemised in the funds flow and paid through payroll at Completion.
  - A specific indemnity for any shortfall, PAYG or super penalties.
- **Recommendation: Insist on deduction and itemisation.** The company, not the Seller, is the employer and would bear the liability after Completion.

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1)
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate." AUD 180k is shown open, with no proof of payment and no confirmatory assignment (DL 4). Clause 7.3 makes title to the Project Materials conditional on cleared payment.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - As a Completion deliverable or CP: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees plus an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay.
  - A specific indemnity covering *all* loss arising from the matter, including third-party and Ironquay infringement claims, re-development and remediation costs.
  - The indemnity outside the cap, basket and disclosure, with a time limit of at least 3–5 years.
  - Optionally, a retention or escrow until the assignment is delivered.
- **Recommendation: Expand the indemnity and require the assignment.** The real risk is that we don't own the code, not the AUD 180k.

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material." Up to about 1,240 personal records were sent to an unintended external address. Access, scope and notifiability have not been determined.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Before signing or Completion:** an updated investigation report, and the Seller procuring that the company completes a Privacy Act Part IIIC (NDB) assessment and makes any required notifications, with Buyer consultation. Note the 30-day assessment window, which has likely already passed if the incident predates 22 Sept.
  - **Specific indemnity** for notification, remediation, forensic and third-party claim costs and regulatory costs, to the extent lawfully indemnifiable. The indemnity should sit outside the cap and basket, with no disclosure defence.
  - A retention or escrow.
  - Removal of the "not expected to be material" characterisation from any warranty or disclosure.
- **Recommendation: Specific indemnity plus retention.** This is a known, unquantified regulatory exposure, so general warranties and disclosure are the wrong tools for it.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k) described as "ordinary-course." The Disclosure Letter itself says they should be "read together" and does not confirm whether each is ordinary course, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Full documents and an explanation of timing.
  - Confirmation of whether the three renewals were split to fall under an approval threshold, and whether Sandbar is a related party.
  - If entered after the locked-box or signing date, or outside ordinary course: treat them as Debt/Transaction Costs or a price adjustment, or require Seller procurement of termination at no cost.
  - A conduct-of-business covenant requiring Buyer consent for commitments over a lower threshold.
- **Recommendation: Do not accept the "ordinary course" label; diligence it, then price it.** The splitting pattern is a red flag.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Seller:** One regime. All limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer wants:** Separate categories, each with its own cap, threshold and time limit:
  1. General Warranties
  2. Fundamental Warranties
  3. Tax Warranties and Tax Indemnity
  4. Specific Indemnities (Ironquay, privacy, bonuses, Riverlark, Sandbar)
  5. Covenant/undertaking claims
  6. Fraud

  Clause 12 limitations should apply only to General Warranty Claims unless expressly stated. Exclusive remedy should not bar termination, specific performance, injunctions, indemnities or fraud claims.
- **Recommendation: Insist on separation.** It is the structural fix that makes every other negotiated protection effective.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification (DD-012)
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced by" the share register at DD-012. DL 10 concedes the Buyer has not completed verification.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Our own diligence:** current ASIC company extract, history of share issues and transfers, constitution, PPSR searches against both Seller and company, and confirmation of no options, convertible notes, ESOP rights or pre-emption rights.
  - **Completion deliverables:** signed transfer, original or replacement certificates, board resolutions approving the transfer and register update, and releases of any share security (including Riverlark if applicable).
  - The title warranty as a Fundamental Warranty (see SPA-N-004).
- **Recommendation: Verify independently; don't rely on the register alone.** A Seller-maintained register is not proof of unencumbered title.

## SPA-N-016: Tax / IP open terms
- **Seller:** These are "settled under the general regime," meaning a 20% cap, 18 months and general disclosure.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Tax:** A stand-alone tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax, including payroll tax and super on the DD-005 bonuses, with:
    - a cap of 100% of price;
    - no de minimis or basket;
    - no disclosure against it;
    - a time limit until the amendment period expires plus a buffer.
  - **IP:** IP warranties covering ownership, no infringement, contractor/employee assignments and open source, with:
    - a higher cap (for example, 50–100%);
    - at least 3 years;
    - Ironquay carved out into its specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation: Treat as OPEN; reject "settled."** For a SaaS target, tax and IP are core value risks, and the general regime under-protects both.

---

## Priority order for the mark-up
1. **Structure:** SPA-N-014, 005, 004 and 006/007. Without these fixes, the specific protections are illusory.
2. **Completion mechanics:** SPA-N-008, 009, 010 and 015.
3. **Specific indemnities and retention:** SPA-N-011 and 012.
4. **Economics:** SPA-N-001, 002, 003, 013 and 016.

**Suggested next steps:**
- Confirm with principals that nothing was agreed at principal level.
- Request the updated DD-006 report, Bluefen correspondence, Riverlark payout figures, Ironquay payment evidence and the Sandbar documents.
- Consider a W&I insurance quote as leverage on the cap and basket.

- **Recommendation: Insist on deduction and itemisation.** The company, not the Seller, is the employer and would bear the liability after Completion.

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1)
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate." AUD 180k is shown open, with no proof of payment and no confirmatory assignment (DL 4). Clause 7.3 makes title to the Project Materials conditional on cleared payment.
- **Buyer wants:**

  - The indemnity outside the cap, basket and disclosure, with a time limit of at least 3–5 years.
  - Optionally, a retention or escrow until the assignment is delivered.

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material." Up to about 1,240 personal records were sent to an unintended external address. Access, scope and notifiability have not been determined.

Note the 30-day assessment window, which has likely already passed if the incident predates 22 Sept.
  - **Specific indemnity** for notification, remediation, forensic and third-party claim costs and regulatory costs, to the extent lawfully indemnifiable. The indemnity should sit outside the cap and basket, with no disclosure defence.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k) described as "ordinary-course." The Disclosure Letter itself says they should be "read together" and does not confirm whether each is ordinary course, terminable or accrued.

  - If entered after the locked-box or signing date, or outside ordinary course: treat them as Debt/Transaction Costs or a price adjustment, or require Seller procurement of termination at no cost.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Seller:** One regime. All limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer wants:** Separate categories, each with its own cap, threshold and time limit:
  1. General Warranties
  2. Fundamental Warranties
  3. Tax Warranties and Tax Indemnity
  4. Specific Indemnities (Ironquay, privacy, bonuses, Riverlark, Sandbar)
  5. Covenant/undertaking claims
  6. Fraud

  Clause 12 limitations should apply only to General Warranty Claims unless expressly stated. Exclusive remedy should not bar termination, specific performance, injunctions, indemnities or fraud claims.
- **Recommendation: Insist on separation.** It is the structural fix that makes every other negotiated protection effective.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification (DD-012)
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced by" the share register at DD-012. DL 10 concedes the Buyer has not completed verification.
- **Buyer wants:**

  - The title warranty as a Fundamental Warranty (see SPA-N-004).
- **Recommendation: Verify independently; don't rely on the register alone.** A Seller-maintained register is not proof of unencumbered title.

## SPA-N-016: Tax / IP open terms
- **Seller:** These are "settled under the general regime," meaning a 20% cap, 18 months and general disclosure.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Tax:** A stand-alone tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax, including payroll tax and super on the DD-005 bonuses, with:
    - a cap of 100% of price;
    - no de minimis or basket;

    - a time limit until the amendment period expires plus a buffer.
  - **IP:** IP warranties covering ownership, no infringement, contractor/employee assignments and open source, with:

    - Ironquay carved out into its specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation: Treat as OPEN; reject "settled."** For a SaaS target, tax and IP are core value risks, and the general regime under-protects both.
